title: Change Explorer — lightweight audit inspector for private deployments (PRD draft)
content:
Context and motivation:

This doc sketches an early PRD for a feature we're calling "Change Explorer" — a compact, queryable audit/forensic inspector for Private deployments (customer-managed VPCs and on-prem bundles). The goal is to let operators and security reviewers quickly understand the provenance and impact of network or config changes that affect inference workloads, to provide explainability for automated approval decisions, and to enable compact evidence export for customer audits and legal discovery.

Why we need this (short):
- Customers on Private and Dedicated repeatedly ask for fast, human-friendly ways to answer "what changed and why did inference latency spike at 02:14 UTC" without having to download terabytes of raw logs.
- Existing PRDs focus on immutable audit storage and high-fidelity traces; but customers want an interactive surface that synthesizes evidence, shows causal chains (change -> approval -> config diff -> metric delta), and exports compact slices.
- This sits between full post-mortem tooling and low-level log archives: the Change Explorer is a curated, indexable view built from sampled audit events, approval tokens, metric deltas, and operator notes.

Primary goals (v1):
1) Quick triage: answer key questions in 30–120s for a single incident window: who approved the change, what was changed, which hosts/pools were affected, and measurable downstream effects (latency, error, cost).
2) Explainability: surface the decision rationale for automated approvals and delegated operator actions (policy reason, matching rule, confidence).
3) Compact forensic export: produce a signed, minimal evidence bundle (JSONL + optional traces) suitable for sharing with customer security teams or SOCs.
4) Privacy-first sampling: keep the default index and exports small while preserving evidentiary integrity (signed digests, references to raw archived logs stored under customer retention policies).

Target users and personas:
- Customer SREs doing incident triage (time-critical)
- Operator on-call inside Redwood (fast root-cause)
- Security/compliance reviewers conducting audits (detailed, periodic)
- Legal/forensics needing exportable artifacts (formal requests)

High-level user flows (v1):
A. Incident Triage (SRE):
- SRE enters a time window or alert id into Change Explorer.
- Explorer returns a ranked list of change candidates (ordered by likelihood to explain metric delta). For each candidate we show: change summary, actor, approval token (signed), affected resource list, brief delta snapshot (latency/cost), and a one-line rationale if automated.
- SRE can click "inspect" to see a lightweight timeline view: approval -> deployment -> metric change -> fallback events.
- SRE can export the evidence bundle (signed) and optionally request full raw-log replay from archival store.

B. Audit / Periodic Review (Security):
- Security reviewer queries by actor/email, by approval gate, or by change type (network ACLs, peering, firewall rules).
- Explorer supports filters and grouping (by customer project, by operator tier).
- Reviewer marks items as "needs follow-up" and adds notes; these notes are appended to the evidence bundle and logged as metadata in the audit index.

C. Explainability check for automated approvals (Product/Policy):
- For any automated approval, Explorer shows the rule match, the scoring/confidence, the historical false-positive rate for that rule, and a concise, human-readable explanation of why the rule fired.

Core data model (conceptual, v1):
- change_event_id: opaque id (indexed)
- timestamp: ISO
- actor: email/or service principal
- change_summary: short text (what changed)
- delta_snapshot: list of metric deltas (latency, error, throughput) — short human-readable lines
- approval_reference: signed token id + gateway (if present)
- affected_topology: short list of entity ids/names (GPUs/pools/agents)
- evidence_refs: pointers to archival objects (s3 path, object id)
- verdict: automated|manual|delegated + optional rationale summary

Note: above is conceptual only. Implementation should avoid embedding full logs in the index; use references and signed digests.

Key requirements (must-have):
- Fast index query latency for narrow time windows (target: median 200ms for single-change lookup).
- Exportable signed bundle format: compact JSONL (max default 10 MB) with manifest and KMS-backed signing.
- Immutable index entries for accepted/archived changes (append-only with versioning metadata).
- Role-based UI filters: operator vs customer auditor see different redacted views per policy.
- SDK/CLI: programmatic query and bundle download endpoints for automation.
- Telemetry: per-query cost, sample fraction used, and evidence bundle size in console.

Nice-to-have (v1 stretch):
- Causal scoring: simple heuristic that scores changes by likelihood-to-explain metric delta (uses correlation and recent deploy metadata).
- Diff visualization for config changes (side-by-side with highlights).
- Quick-replay button to request a raw-logs replay for that change (async job).

Data retention and sampling model (proposal):
- Index rows (Change Explorer entries) are kept at least for 90 days by default (customer-configurable to 365/730).
- Raw log references retained according to the customer's Private retention policy — Explorer stores only signed digests and references.
- Sampling: system keeps full fidelity for approved changes in the last 7 days; beyond that we down-sample event traces (keep top N traces per change, where N default = 3).
- Compact export defaults: include index rows + top N traces + cert chain. Option to include a full-log URL token (requires customer permission/key).

Approval gate integrations and explainability hooks:
- Approval systems must emit a small "explain" payload whenever a rule triggers: rule_id, matched_inputs (redacted), score/confidence, and snippet describing why accepted/denied. Explorer must index that payload and surface it inline.
- For delegated operator approvals, include delegation chain and escalation references.

Security and privacy considerations:
- All exported bundles are signed by Redwood's export signing key and include a per-bundle nonce. Customers can request HSM-backed signatures for high-sensitivity exports.
- Sensitive fields (IP addresses, internal hostnames) are redacted by default unless the requesting principal has explicit permission. Redaction policy must be configurable per-customer.
- Explorer must enforce consented export: if raw logs are required, include an explicit customer opt-in and audit entry for the export request.

Operational cost model (rough):
- Indexing pipeline cost per 1k change events: small; main cost is storage of traces and archive retrieval.
- Exporting a full-log bundle (not default compact) should trigger a chargeable retrieval; surface the cost estimate in UI.

UI/UX sketch (notes):
- Top-of-page search bar (alert-id, change-id, actor).
- Ranked candidates pane (center) with change cards. Each card shows one-line summary, time, actor, approval badge (auto/manual), severity score, and quick-actions (inspect, export, add-note).
- Details panel (right) with timeline, affected topology, pre/post metric micro-snapshot, approval explanation, and evidence references.
- Audit mode: filter bar (by gate, by actor, by resource), bulk-marking, export queue.

API surfaces (v1):
- GET /explorer/query?since=&until=&actor=&resource= -> list of change rows (paginated)
- GET /explorer/change/{id} -> detailed row + signed manifest
- POST /explorer/export (change_ids[], format=compact|full) -> export job id
- GET /explorer/export/{id} -> signed bundle url (when ready)
- CLI: redwood explorer query --window 2025-02-03T01:00Z --id JIRA-1222 -> prints candidate summary

Open implementation questions / risks:
1) Index costs for very chatty customers — need guardrails: retention tiers / sampling / per-customer quotas.
2) Proving provenance on partial samples: how to prove an exported compact bundle is representative if we only include top-N traces? Need manifest with signed digests of archival objects to prove non-tampering.
3) Redaction complexity: some customers will want full hostnames; others will demand IP removal. We need a per-customer redaction policy in config.
4) UX: how to surface automated-rule confidence without causing too many follow-up tickets (show historical FP rates, help interpret).
5) SLA: queries should be fast; heavier exports async. We need SRE guidance on indexing and cache TTLs.

Acceptance criteria (v1):
- MVP service deployed behind Private control plane with UI flyout in Console and CLI surface.
- Can answer top 5 triage questions for 80% of incidents within 2 minutes using default sampling and index.
- Signed compact export manifest generated and verifiable with archived digests.
- RBAC redaction enforced end-to-end.

Rollout plan and milestones (proposal):
- Sprint 0 (2 weeks): finalize event schema and export manifest format. Wireframe UI and API contract.
- Sprint 1 (4 weeks): indexing pipeline + small query API + proof-of-concept UI with mock data.
- Sprint 2 (4 weeks): approval-explain payload ingestion, export signing, basic RBAC redaction, CLI.
- Pilot (4 weeks): onboard 1–2 security-conscious customers + internal SREs, collect feedback.

Metrics to track:
- query p95 latency, median latency (target median <250ms for single-id lookup)
- % incidents where Explorer returned correct top-1 candidate (measured in pilot)
- export bundle sizes and frequency
- number of export requests requiring full-log retrieval (cost signal)

Notes / TODOs:
- Draft proto for manifest + signing (Rajat)
- Wire up minimal UI sketch in console (Liam)
- Acquire customer pilot candidates (CS lead: Evelyn)
- Security review of redaction model and HSM signing (security team)

References and related docs:
- private-deploy-change-authorization-checkpoints-prd-draft.json (related background)
- compact-manifest-offline-delivery-prd-draft.json (export format ideas)
- approval-explainability-and-evidence-summaries-prd-rough.json (overlap on explainability; ensure we avoid duplication by narrowing to the "inspector/export" surface)

Unresolved: exact manifest fields and signing protocol (must finalize with infra/security). Also need to decide default sampling policy (3 traces vs 5) before engineering kickoff.

Bottom line:
Change Explorer should give Private customers and our SREs a fast, defensible way to reason about change provenance and impact without forcing them to wade through full archives. The focus is compact, signed evidence + human explanation for both manual and automated approvals.

----
Working notes / scratch (keep short):
- Example one-line card: [2025-02-12T02:13Z] operator: maya.rivera@custco.com — "changed edge-nat ACL for pool-gpu-3" — approval: delegated-operator (escalation=off) — latency +150ms in pool-gpu-3
- Export manifest sketch: manifest{bundle_id, signer, change_ids:[], index_hashes:[], trace_refs:[], redaction_policy, generated_at} (TBD exact shape)
- Licensing: include mention that export of full logs may be billable for Private tenants (billing config).

End of draft.

Feedback welcome — want to finalize schema & manifest before next PM sync.
